artboards.title: Midway 10:25 · a fleet battle in its own century
The moves, and the fifth slot

annotations.text:
THE STAFF-MAP VIEW (#139), RESOLVED 2026-09-07 — the first view built outside the engraved system. ADR-0021 fixed the rule it works to: what the picture shows, where each thing sits and what it means is the same in every view; HOW any of it is drawn is the view's. So every board here is one hand redrawing an unchanged anatomy — same extent and north up, same furniture in the same corners, same caption band with the clock at the left, same label on the flank, same four states, same 72 px glyph, same side ink by roster order.
The chips open on what was CHOSEN — candidate A for the glyph, the tapered arrow for the moves, Archivo for the face, the lightened sea — and the unchosen candidates stay behind them. The GROUND is not reopened: #138 chose the `ops` sheet and it is imported unchanged.

WHAT EACH FRAME IS FOR. TRAFALGAR 13:30 is the overlap test every view passes — eight units, four of them locked together in the same 200 px, which is where a glyph that looked handsome alone stops reading. CANNAE asks whether a twentieth-century idiom on a 216 BC battle is absurd or clarifying; the marks are the ones a reader already brings (crossed diagonals for foot, one for horse), and the ground is #138's. MIDWAY is the case the engraved plate serves worst: open ocean, where a graticule is the only thing that says where anything is.
Nothing is geo-registered — as on the terrain canvas, these are scenes, not map files.

ONE THING #138 COULD NOT HAVE SEEN, now settled. Its water tone was chosen against a sliver of sea on a land battle; Midway is the first frame that is water edge to edge, and at full frame `#93a9b6` read as a blue sheet rather than a buff one with sea on it. DECIDED: open water is lightened to `#b3c4cb`, and `#93a9b6` becomes the shallow and reef tone — a correction to the chosen `ops` palette, not a reopening of it. The old tone stays on the chip.

DECIDED, 2026-09-07. The chips open on what was chosen; the unchosen candidates stay behind them.
1 · THE GLYPH: A, the frame to frontage — the box IS the unit's 72 px footprint.
2 · THE MOVES: the tapered operations arrow, which cannot come out of a `Pen`. ADR-0021's fifth slot is CUT: a view supplies a `moves` hand of three functions, and the engraved three wrap the arrow they already draw.
3 · THE FACE: Archivo at wdth 75 — the only variable one of the three, so one file carries the condensed width and both weights.
4 · THE LEADER: the elbow ending in a tick, owned by `type`, so the label pass still gains no slot of its own.
5 · THE NAME: Staff map.
6 · THE SEA: lightened at full frame.
NOT this ticket: the aircraft sign (#140, blocked on #131) is a candidate only; the player's controls and chooser are #137's; the ground is #138's, closed.
